review.summary: RC16 independently reviewed 41 changed Go files for gallery previews, bounded file receiving, telemetry isolation and release metadata. No new third-party import paths, generated protobuf or source symlinks were found. Exact Go 1.27.2 observation covers six production targets, 917 first-party files and 106 production modules; Linux closures add five production GoFiles. Excluded not-in-production modules remain absent. Module manifests, upstream torrent source and build targets are unchanged; existing findings and expiry remain unchanged. Full L3 must recompute actual/original closure identity and all scanners. File-share large-file candidate requalification: content-bound sharing grows to 10 GiB with independent legacy upload limits and bounded proof deadlines; no dependency or build-target changes. All changed Go source and direct callers independently reviewed. Six-platform closure identity must be recomputed against the unchanged recorded closure before delivery. File-share timeout follow-up independently reviewed: share-only DeadlineExceeded maps to retryable504 through Agent/Panel/UI, with no new production imports/packages or dependency/build changes. All prior findings and expiry remain unchanged; official six-platform closure revalidation is required. RC17 assembly retains the independently reviewed large-file share production tree; the only additional Go change is the release version string. Existing closure, findings and expiry are unchanged and full canonical L3 revalidates them. RC18: release reviewer independently reviewed all four changed workspace/Panel Go sources and version metadata; command strings are inert bounded workspace data, remote target intent fails closed, existing authenticated terminal API is reused. No new production files/imports, dependency graph, generated code, symlinks or build target changes. Closure, findings and expiry unchanged; full canonical L3 recomputes identity. RC18 closeout test-only qualification: MCP preflight test now holds a controlled channel barrier and waits for the durable asynchronous terminal state, asserting the exact revocation error and zero writes. Every production Go path/hash remains identical to independently reviewed published RC18; only one existing test file changed, with no imports/dependencies/build targets/production closure/findings/expiry changes. New test reviewed by release fixture maintainer; no new independent test-review claim. Shoutrrr multi-channel candidate: independently reviewed all changed notification Go source and adapter boundaries; six-platform actual/original closures match, 926 first-party files and 110 production modules. Added production modules are shoutrrr v0.8.0, fatih/color v1.19.0, go-colorable v0.1.14 and go-isatty v0.0.24. Existing excluded modules remain outside production and superseded versions remain unchanged. Findings, observation dates, expiry, upstream source and build targets are unchanged. Official inventory qualification, source scanners and L2 must revalidate this observation before delivery. Notification usability follow-up: generic channel state naming retains all legacy JSON fields and aliases, with a JSON compatibility regression test. No new imports, modules, production Go filenames or build target changes; closure and existing findings/expiry are unchanged. Independent source review passed; canonical Linux inventory qualification and L2 remain required. RC19 release assembly independently reviewed; the only extra Go change is version metadata. Existing independently reviewed Shoutrrr closure, findings and expiry remain; full L3 requalifies six targets and scanners. RC20 assembly independently reviewed: bounded inert theme ZIP installation retains existing opaque capability sandbox; fixed-provider authenticated tutorial discovery reuses existing thumbnail allowlists and bounded cache. Six-platform observation retains all 110 production modules and selected versions, with only tutorial_feed.go and upload.go added to existing Linux production package GoFiles. 930 first-party files qualified. Existing findings, upstream identity, build targets, observation and expiry remain unchanged. Full canonical L3/scanners remain required; CF scoped deferred before stable. Retained terminal integration independently reviewed: no new third-party imports, modules, build targets, generated source or symlinks. Six-platform observation retains 110 production modules and adds terminal_retained.go only to the existing Linux cluster package. First-party source and closure are rebound; findings and expiry are unchanged. Canonical actual/original inventory qualification and full L2 remain required before integration; scoped CF audit remains deferred before release. Terminal retention compatibility follow-up independently reviewed existing production/test files: only a standard-library errors import is added; no new third-party imports, modules, build files, generated source or symlinks. Existing production GoFiles and six-platform closure identity remain unchanged. First-party source identity is rebound with independent evidence; canonical actual/original inventories and L2 must pass before integration. Findings, observation date and expiry remain unchanged. Lost-launch close follow-up independently reviewed: authenticated, bounded, server-issued launch intents fence delayed shortcut starts; existing user/host/shortcut ownership and input fences are retained. Only standard-library test imports added; no production GoFiles, third-party modules, build, generated source or symlink changes. Source identity rebound with independent evidence; canonical six-platform and final L2/CI required before integration. Existing findings and expiry unchanged. Local app-market candidate (author-qualified, independent review pending): adds local_apps.go to the existing Linux internal/appmarket package to list trusted /root/apps-local kejilion.sh configs; only standard-library imports, no new third-party modules, build targets, generated source or symlinks. Six-platform closure and first-party source (937 files) were recomputed by the author with the canonical method, which reproduces the recorded base identity exactly; independent review must confirm before integration. Existing findings and expiry unchanged.
